record.context_brief: graphs and combinatorial torus structures admitting affine complements
record.original_question: Find graphs whose complements admit affine structures. More specifically, in each dimension there should be only finitely many such graphs and finitely many corresponding combinatorial torus structures whose complements admit affine structures; can these objects be classified?

evidence.quote: Question 2.19. Find graphs whose complements admit affine structures. In fact, there is a finite number of such graphs in each dimension. There should be a finite number of such combinatorial torus structures whose compliments admit affine structures. This is the first challenging question. Classify them if possible.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A combinatorial torus structure of dimension n is a simplicial (or cubical/PL) decomposition of the n-dimensional torus T^n = R^n/Z^n, with associated 1-skeleton viewed as a finite graph G embedded in T^n. The complement T^n \ G of such a graph in the torus is said to admit an affine structure if it can be endowed with an atlas of charts to R^n whose transition maps are restrictions of affine transformations of R^n (equivalently, a (Aff(R^n), R^n)-structure).

The problem is the following:

(a) Show that, for each fixed dimension n, there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of finite graphs G that arise as the 1-skeleton of a combinatorial torus structure on T^n whose complement T^n \ G admits an affine structure.

(b) Show that, for each fixed dimension n, there are only finitely many such combinatorial torus structures (up to combinatorial equivalence) whose complements admit affine structures.

(c) Give an explicit classification of all such graphs and combinatorial torus structures.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published classification or finiteness proof matching this question about graphs in tori whose complements admit affine structures. Related topics (toric arrangements, integral affine structures on spheres, Heawood-type graphs) appear in the literature, but no source confirms the specific finiteness statements or classification posed here. The status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Integral affine structures on spheres and torus fibrations of Calabi-Yau toric hypersurfaces I
status_evidence.snippet: Describes in purely combinatorial terms dual pairs of integral affine structures on spheres coming from mirror families of Calabi-Yau toric hypersurfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on combinatorial/affine structures exists but does not address the specific classification of graphs in T^n with affine complements.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Heawood Graphs (arXiv:2307.11859)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies toroidal graphs generalizing the Heawood graph.
status_evidence.claim: Combinatorial graphs on tori are studied, but no classification result for affine-complement graphs is given.
